methods.label: Multiple imputation (m at least 20, more when more rows are incomplete)
methods.customary: Customary in epidemiology (Sterne et al. 2009, BMJ 338:b2393)

methods.label: Complete cases
methods.customary: Customary in epidemiology; most software's default
methods.sound: Sound if complete cases give unbiased coefficients only if whether a value is missing does not depend on the outcome, given the predictors (Groenwold et al. 2012; White & Carlin 2010); it costs every incomplete row.

methods.label: Single fill in each training fold
methods.customary: Customary in machine-learning pipelines (scikit-learn's SimpleImputer)

methods.label: Single fill with missing indicators

exposure_forms.label: Restricted cubic spline

exposure_forms.label: Straight line
exposure_forms.customary: Customary: one coefficient per unit of intake.
exposure_forms.sound: Sound when the relation is close to a line; a curve it misses biases the slope.
exposure_forms.consequence: One coefficient per unit; no curvature.

exposure_forms.label: Quintiles with a trend test
exposure_forms.customary: Customary in nutritional epidemiology: "quintiles remain expected alongside" the spline (NUTRITION_PACK §07G).
exposure_forms.sound: Weaker for inference: cutting a continuous intake into fifths discards the variation within each fifth and assumes a step at each cut; the trend test scores each fifth by its median.
exposure_forms.consequence: Four indicators against the lowest fifth, and a trend across medians.

missing.tension: Complete cases are the field's habit; when the blanks depend on measured variables they may be biased, and multiple imputation with the outcome is sounder (Sterne et al. 2009, BMJ 338:b2393).

exposure_forms.label: Restricted cubic spline
exposure_forms.customary: Increasingly customary in nutritional epidemiology: "now near-default" (NUTRITION_PACK §07G; Desquilbet & Mariotti 2010).
exposure_forms.sound: Sound: a smooth curve with few parameters, linear in the tails, with a test of nonlinearity; knots at Harrell's percentiles of the fitting rows.
exposure_forms.consequence: Adds a curve's terms per exposure and a test of whether it bends.

exposure_forms.label: Straight line
exposure_forms.customary: Customary: one coefficient per unit of intake.
exposure_forms.sound: Sound when the relation is close to a line; a curve it misses biases the slope.
exposure_forms.consequence: One coefficient per unit; no curvature.

exposure_forms.label: Quintiles with a trend test
exposure_forms.customary: Customary in nutritional epidemiology: "quintiles remain expected alongside" the spline (NUTRITION_PACK §07G).
exposure_forms.sound: Weaker for inference: cutting a continuous intake into fifths discards the variation within each fifth and assumes a step at each cut; the trend test scores each fifth by its median.
exposure_forms.consequence: Four indicators against the lowest fifth, and a trend across medians.

imputation_models.sound: Unsound on clustered rows: imputing clustered rows one at a time gives a unit's time-invariant values different draws on its different rows and erases the correlation within units (Lüdtke, Robitzsch & Grund 2017)

missing.question: missing

options.label: Multiple imputation (m at least 20, more when more rows are incomplete)

customary.text: Customary in epidemiology (Sterne et al. 2009, BMJ 338:b2393)

sound.reason: Sound: with the outcome and energy in the imputation model it is unbiased under missing at random and its intervals carry the imputation's uncertainty (Moons et al. 2006).

customary.text: Customary in epidemiology; most software's default
customary.source: Sterne et al. 2009, BMJ 338:b2393: "Researchers usually address missing data by including in the analysis only complete cases"

sound.reason: Sound if complete cases give unbiased coefficients only if whether a value is missing does not depend on the outcome, given the predictors (Groenwold et al. 2012; White & Carlin 2010); it costs every incomplete row.

options.label: Single fill in each training fold

customary.text: Customary in machine-learning pipelines (scikit-learn's SimpleImputer)
customary.source: scikit-learn's SimpleImputer, the pipelines' default fill

sound.reason: Unsound for an interval: a single fill treats each imputed value as measured, so the intervals are too narrow, and a median fill biases a coefficient whenever who is missing depends on another variable.

customary.text: Customary in prediction from health records (Sperrin et al. 2020)
customary.source: Sperrin et al. 2020, J Clin Epidemiol 125:183

sound.reason: Unsound for an estimate: the missing-indicator method almost always biases the estimates of a nonrandomized study (Groenwold et al. 2012); it is valid for baseline covariates in a randomized trial.

customary.text: Customary for questions not asked (a blank medication answer)
customary.source: NUTRITION_PACK §06 (a blank that means not asked)

sound.reason: The missing-indicator method for categories: the missing-indicator method almost always biases the estimates of a nonrandomized study (Groenwold et al. 2012); it is valid for baseline covariates in a randomized trial; sound when a blank means not asked (then it is a value, not missing).

missing.tension: Complete cases are the field's habit; when the blanks depend on measured variables they may be biased, and multiple imputation with the outcome is sounder (Sterne et al. 2009, BMJ 338:b2393).

exposure_forms.label: Restricted cubic spline
exposure_forms.customary: Increasingly customary in nutritional epidemiology: "now near-default" (NUTRITION_PACK §07G; Desquilbet & Mariotti 2010).
exposure_forms.sound: Sound: a smooth curve with few parameters, linear in the tails, with a test of nonlinearity; knots at Harrell's percentiles of the fitting rows.
exposure_forms.consequence: Adds a curve's terms per exposure and a test of whether it bends.

exposure_forms.label: Straight line
exposure_forms.customary: Customary: one coefficient per unit of intake.
exposure_forms.sound: Sound when the relation is close to a line; a curve it misses biases the slope.
exposure_forms.consequence: One coefficient per unit; no curvature.

exposure_forms.label: Quintiles with a trend test
exposure_forms.customary: Customary in nutritional epidemiology: "quintiles remain expected alongside" the spline (NUTRITION_PACK §07G).
exposure_forms.sound: Weaker for inference: cutting a continuous intake into fifths discards the variation within each fifth and assumes a step at each cut; the trend test scores each fifth by its median.
exposure_forms.consequence: Four indicators against the lowest fifth, and a trend across medians.

families.label: Linear model
families.inductive_bias: Each predictor adds a straight-line effect; effects add up, with no interactions unless you build them.

families.label: Elastic net
concerns: Penalized coefficients are shrunk and carry no confidence intervals.
families.inductive_bias: Straight-line effects shrunk toward zero; few predictors matter, correlated ones share weight.

families.label: Feature-wise regression
concerns: Each exposure is adjusted for the covariates but not for the other exposures: a separate question for each.
families.inductive_bias: Each exposure tested on its own with the covariates; Benjamini–Hochberg holds the false-discovery rate.

families.label: Boosted trees
concerns: No coefficients or intervals: effects are read from curves instead.
families.inductive_bias: Effects are step functions that can bend and interact; many shallow trees each correct the last.

families.label: Random-intercept mixed model
concerns: No identifier repeats in these rows, so there is no unit for a random intercept; it is the linear model's fit.
families.inductive_bias: Straight-line effects, plus a level of its own for each unit whose rows repeat.

families.label: GEE (exchangeable)
concerns: No identifier repeats in these rows, so there is no within-unit correlation to model; it is the linear model's fit.
families.inductive_bias: Population-average straight-line or log-odds effects; a unit's rows share one correlation.

families.label: Screened elastic net
concerns: Screening chooses the reported features from the outcome: under inference that is selection, refused for the reported model.
families.inductive_bias: Only features with a strong marginal association survive; among them, straight-line effects shrunk toward zero.

methods.label: Multiple imputation (m at least 20, more when more rows are incomplete)
methods.customary: Customary in epidemiology (Sterne et al. 2009, BMJ 338:b2393)
methods.sound: Sound: with the outcome and energy in the imputation model it is unbiased under missing at random and its intervals carry the imputation's uncertainty (Moons et al. 2006).

methods.label: Complete cases
methods.customary: Customary in epidemiology; most software's default
methods.sound: Sound if complete cases give unbiased coefficients only if whether a value is missing does not depend on the outcome, given the predictors (Groenwold et al. 2012; White & Carlin 2010); it costs every incomplete row.

methods.label: Single fill in each training fold
methods.customary: Customary in machine-learning pipelines (scikit-learn's SimpleImputer)
methods.sound: Unsound for an interval: a single fill treats each imputed value as measured, so the intervals are too narrow, and a median fill biases a coefficient whenever who is missing depends on another variable.

methods.label: Single fill with missing indicators
methods.customary: Customary in prediction from health records (Sperrin et al. 2020)
methods.sound: Unsound for an estimate: the missing-indicator method almost always biases the estimates of a nonrandomized study (Groenwold et al. 2012); it is valid for baseline covariates in a randomized trial.

methods.label: Blanks as their own level
methods.customary: Customary for questions not asked (a blank medication answer)
methods.sound: The missing-indicator method for categories: the missing-indicator method almost always biases the estimates of a nonrandomized study (Groenwold et al. 2012); it is valid for baseline covariates in a randomized trial; sound when a blank means not asked (then it is a value, not missing).

below_detection.label: Censoring-aware
below_detection.customary: Less common in metabolomics; the epidemiology of exposures below detection (Lubin et al. 2004)
below_detection.sound: Sound for associations. A censored-normal (Tobit) draw below the limit within the multiple imputation, given the outcome (Lubin et al. 2004).

below_detection.label: Half the smallest detected value
below_detection.sound: Biased for associations as censoring grows, and collapses every non-detect to one value (Lubin et al. 2004: biased unless 5–10% are below the limit).

below_detection.label: As any other blank (the median fill)
below_detection.sound: Unsound: the median places non-detections in the middle of the distribution.

imputation_models.label: Compatible with the analysis model (SMC-FCS where the model needs it)
imputation_models.customary: Chained equations with derived terms made in each copy (passive) are the field's habit (mice's and Stata's defaults)
imputation_models.sound: Sound: SMC-FCS where the model holds a spline, a log, a ratio or a logistic or Cox outcome, chained equations where it is linear in the imputed values (Bartlett et al. 2015)

imputation_models.label: Passive: terms derived in each completed copy
imputation_models.customary: Customary: mice's and Stata's ice defaults derive transformed and product terms in each completed copy
imputation_models.sound: Unsound with a declared nonlinear term: passive imputation draws each value from a model linear in it and only then derives the declared nonlinear terms, so the curvature and the nonlinearity tests would be biased toward the null (Bartlett et al. 2015)

imputation_models.label: Single-level on clustered rows
imputation_models.customary: Customary: chained equations that ignore the clustering
imputation_models.sound: Unsound on clustered rows: imputing clustered rows one at a time gives a unit's time-invariant values different draws on its different rows and erases the correlation within units (Lüdtke, Robitzsch & Grund 2017)

families.label: Feature-wise regression

families.label: Boosted trees
concerns: No coefficients or intervals: effects are read from curves instead.
families.inductive_bias: Effects are step functions that can bend and interact; many shallow trees each correct the last.

families.label: Random-intercept mixed model
concerns: No identifier repeats in these rows, so there is no unit for a random intercept; it is the linear model's fit.
families.inductive_bias: Straight-line effects, plus a level of its own for each unit whose rows repeat.

families.label: GEE (exchangeable)
concerns: No identifier repeats in these rows, so there is no within-unit correlation to model; it is the linear model's fit.
families.inductive_bias: Population-average straight-line or log-odds effects; a unit's rows share one correlation.

families.label: Screened elastic net
concerns: Screening chooses the reported features from the outcome: under inference that is selection, refused for the reported model.
families.inductive_bias: Only features with a strong marginal association survive; among them, straight-line effects shrunk toward zero.

methods.label: Multiple imputation (m at least 20, more when more rows are incomplete)
methods.customary: Customary in epidemiology (Sterne et al. 2009, BMJ 338:b2393)
methods.sound: Sound: with the outcome and energy in the imputation model it is unbiased under missing at random and its intervals carry the imputation's uncertainty (Moons et al. 2006).

methods.label: Complete cases
methods.customary: Customary in epidemiology; most software's default
methods.sound: Sound if complete cases give unbiased coefficients only if whether a value is missing does not depend on the outcome, given the predictors (Groenwold et al. 2012; White & Carlin 2010); it costs every incomplete row.

methods.label: Single fill in each training fold
methods.customary: Customary in machine-learning pipelines (scikit-learn's SimpleImputer)
methods.sound: Unsound for an interval: a single fill treats each imputed value as measured, so the intervals are too narrow, and a median fill biases a coefficient whenever who is missing depends on another variable.

methods.label: Single fill with missing indicators
methods.customary: Customary in prediction from health records (Sperrin et al. 2020)
methods.sound: Unsound for an estimate: the missing-indicator method almost always biases the estimates of a nonrandomized study (Groenwold et al. 2012); it is valid for baseline covariates in a randomized trial.

methods.label: Blanks as their own level
methods.customary: Customary for questions not asked (a blank medication answer)
methods.sound: The missing-indicator method for categories: the missing-indicator method almost always biases the estimates of a nonrandomized study (Groenwold et al. 2012); it is valid for baseline covariates in a randomized trial; sound when a blank means not asked (then it is a value, not missing).

below_detection.label: Censoring-aware
below_detection.customary: Less common in metabolomics; the epidemiology of exposures below detection (Lubin et al. 2004)
below_detection.sound: Sound for associations. A censored-normal (Tobit) draw below the limit within the multiple imputation, given the outcome (Lubin et al. 2004).

below_detection.label: Half the smallest detected value
below_detection.sound: Biased for associations as censoring grows, and collapses every non-detect to one value (Lubin et al. 2004: biased unless 5–10% are below the limit).

below_detection.label: As any other blank (the median fill)
below_detection.sound: Unsound: the median places non-detections in the middle of the distribution.

imputation_models.label: Compatible with the analysis model (SMC-FCS where the model needs it)
imputation_models.customary: Chained equations with derived terms made in each copy (passive) are the field's habit (mice's and Stata's defaults)
imputation_models.sound: Sound: SMC-FCS where the model holds a spline, a log, a ratio or a logistic or Cox outcome, chained equations where it is linear in the imputed values (Bartlett et al. 2015)

imputation_models.label: Passive: terms derived in each completed copy
imputation_models.customary: Customary: mice's and Stata's ice defaults derive transformed and product terms in each completed copy
imputation_models.sound: Unsound with a declared nonlinear term: passive imputation draws each value from a model linear in it and only then derives the declared nonlinear terms, so the curvature and the nonlinearity tests would be biased toward the null (Bartlett et al. 2015)

imputation_models.label: Single-level on clustered rows
imputation_models.customary: Customary: chained equations that ignore the clustering
imputation_models.sound: Unsound on clustered rows: imputing clustered rows one at a time gives a unit's time-invariant values different draws on its different rows and erases the correlation within units (Lüdtke, Robitzsch & Grund 2017)

exposure_forms.label: Restricted cubic spline
exposure_forms.customary: Increasingly customary in nutritional epidemiology: "now near-default" (NUTRITION_PACK §07G; Desquilbet & Mariotti 2010).
exposure_forms.sound: Sound: a smooth curve with few parameters, linear in the tails, with a test of nonlinearity; knots at Harrell's percentiles of the fitting rows.
exposure_forms.consequence: Adds a curve's terms per exposure and a test of whether it bends.

exposure_forms.label: Straight line
exposure_forms.customary: Customary: one coefficient per unit of intake.
exposure_forms.sound: Sound when the relation is close to a line; a curve it misses biases the slope.
exposure_forms.consequence: One coefficient per unit; no curvature.

exposure_forms.label: Quintiles with a trend test
exposure_forms.customary: Customary in nutritional epidemiology: "quintiles remain expected alongside" the spline (NUTRITION_PACK §07G).
exposure_forms.sound: Weaker for inference: cutting a continuous intake into fifths discards the variation within each fifth and assumes a step at each cut; the trend test scores each fifth by its median.
exposure_forms.consequence: Four indicators against the lowest fifth, and a trend across medians.

families.label: Linear model
families.inductive_bias: Each predictor adds a straight-line effect; effects add up, with no interactions unless you build them.

families.label: Elastic net
concerns: Penalized coefficients are shrunk and carry no confidence intervals.
families.inductive_bias: Straight-line effects shrunk toward zero; few predictors matter, correlated ones share weight.

families.label: Feature-wise regression
concerns: Each exposure is adjusted for the covariates but not for the other exposures: a separate question for each.
families.inductive_bias: Each exposure tested on its own with the covariates; Benjamini–Hochberg holds the false-discovery rate.

families.label: Boosted trees
concerns: No coefficients or intervals: effects are read from curves instead.
families.inductive_bias: Effects are step functions that can bend and interact; many shallow trees each correct the last.

families.label: Random-intercept mixed model
concerns: No identifier repeats in these rows, so there is no unit for a random intercept; it is the linear model's fit.
families.inductive_bias: Straight-line effects, plus a level of its own for each unit whose rows repeat.

families.label: GEE (exchangeable)
concerns: No identifier repeats in these rows, so there is no within-unit correlation to model; it is the linear model's fit.
families.inductive_bias: Population-average straight-line or log-odds effects; a unit's rows share one correlation.

families.label: Screened elastic net
concerns: Screening chooses the reported features from the outcome: under inference that is selection, refused for the reported model.
families.inductive_bias: Only features with a strong marginal association survive; among them, straight-line effects shrunk toward zero.

methods.label: Multiple imputation (m at least 20, more when more rows are incomplete)
methods.customary: Customary in epidemiology (Sterne et al. 2009, BMJ 338:b2393)
methods.sound: Sound: with the outcome and energy in the imputation model it is unbiased under missing at random and its intervals carry the imputation's uncertainty (Moons et al. 2006).

methods.label: Complete cases
methods.customary: Customary in epidemiology; most software's default
methods.sound: Sound if complete cases give unbiased coefficients only if whether a value is missing does not depend on the outcome, given the predictors (Groenwold et al. 2012; White & Carlin 2010); it costs every incomplete row.

methods.label: Single fill in each training fold
methods.customary: Customary in machine-learning pipelines (scikit-learn's SimpleImputer)
methods.sound: Unsound for an interval: a single fill treats each imputed value as measured, so the intervals are too narrow, and a median fill biases a coefficient whenever who is missing depends on another variable.

methods.label: Single fill with missing indicators
methods.customary: Customary in prediction from health records (Sperrin et al. 2020)
methods.sound: Unsound for an estimate: the missing-indicator method almost always biases the estimates of a nonrandomized study (Groenwold et al. 2012); it is valid for baseline covariates in a randomized trial.

methods.label: Blanks as their own level
methods.customary: Customary for questions not asked (a blank medication answer)
methods.sound: The missing-indicator method for categories: the missing-indicator method almost always biases the estimates of a nonrandomized study (Groenwold et al. 2012); it is valid for baseline covariates in a randomized trial; sound when a blank means not asked (then it is a value, not missing).

below_detection.label: Censoring-aware
below_detection.customary: Less common in metabolomics; the epidemiology of exposures below detection (Lubin et al. 2004)
below_detection.sound: Sound for associations. A censored-normal (Tobit) draw below the limit within the multiple imputation, given the outcome (Lubin et al. 2004).

below_detection.label: Half the smallest detected value
below_detection.sound: Biased for associations as censoring grows, and collapses every non-detect to one value (Lubin et al. 2004: biased unless 5–10% are below the limit).

below_detection.label: As any other blank (the median fill)
below_detection.sound: Unsound: the median places non-detections in the middle of the distribution.

imputation_models.label: Compatible with the analysis model (SMC-FCS where the model needs it)
imputation_models.customary: Chained equations with derived terms made in each copy (passive) are the field's habit (mice's and Stata's defaults)
imputation_models.sound: Sound: SMC-FCS where the model holds a spline, a log, a ratio or a logistic or Cox outcome, chained equations where it is linear in the imputed values (Bartlett et al. 2015)

imputation_models.label: Passive: terms derived in each completed copy
imputation_models.customary: Customary: mice's and Stata's ice defaults derive transformed and product terms in each completed copy
imputation_models.sound: Unsound with a declared nonlinear term: passive imputation draws each value from a model linear in it and only then derives the declared nonlinear terms, so the curvature and the nonlinearity tests would be biased toward the null (Bartlett et al. 2015)

imputation_models.label: Single-level on clustered rows
imputation_models.customary: Customary: chained equations that ignore the clustering
imputation_models.sound: Unsound on clustered rows: imputing clustered rows one at a time gives a unit's time-invariant values different draws on its different rows and erases the correlation within units (Lüdtke, Robitzsch & Grund 2017)

exposure_forms.label: Restricted cubic spline
exposure_forms.customary: Increasingly customary in nutritional epidemiology: "now near-default" (NUTRITION_PACK §07G; Desquilbet & Mariotti 2010).
exposure_forms.sound: Sound: a smooth curve with few parameters, linear in the tails, with a test of nonlinearity; knots at Harrell's percentiles of the fitting rows.
exposure_forms.consequence: Adds a curve's terms per exposure and a test of whether it bends.

exposure_forms.label: Straight line
exposure_forms.customary: Customary: one coefficient per unit of intake.
exposure_forms.sound: Sound when the relation is close to a line; a curve it misses biases the slope.
exposure_forms.consequence: One coefficient per unit; no curvature.

exposure_forms.label: Quintiles with a trend test
exposure_forms.customary: Customary in nutritional epidemiology: "quintiles remain expected alongside" the spline (NUTRITION_PACK §07G).
exposure_forms.sound: Weaker for inference: cutting a continuous intake into fifths discards the variation within each fifth and assumes a step at each cut; the trend test scores each fifth by its median.
exposure_forms.consequence: Four indicators against the lowest fifth, and a trend across medians.

families.label: Linear model
families.inductive_bias: Each predictor adds a straight-line effect; effects add up, with no interactions unless you build them.

families.label: Elastic net
concerns: Penalized coefficients are shrunk and carry no confidence intervals.
families.inductive_bias: Straight-line effects shrunk toward zero; few predictors matter, correlated ones share weight.

families.label: Feature-wise regression
concerns: Each exposure is adjusted for the covariates but not for the other exposures: a separate question for each.
families.inductive_bias: Each exposure tested on its own with the covariates; Benjamini–Hochberg holds the false-discovery rate.

families.label: Boosted trees
concerns: No coefficients or intervals: effects are read from curves instead.
families.inductive_bias: Effects are step functions that can bend and interact; many shallow trees each correct the last.

families.label: Random-intercept mixed model
concerns: No identifier repeats in these rows, so there is no unit for a random intercept; it is the linear model's fit.
families.inductive_bias: Straight-line effects, plus a level of its own for each unit whose rows repeat.

families.label: GEE (exchangeable)
concerns: No identifier repeats in these rows, so there is no within-unit correlation to model; it is the linear model's fit.
families.inductive_bias: Population-average straight-line or log-odds effects; a unit's rows share one correlation.

families.label: Screened elastic net
concerns: Screening chooses the reported features from the outcome: under inference that is selection, refused for the reported model.
families.inductive_bias: Only features with a strong marginal association survive; among them, straight-line effects shrunk toward zero.

methods.label: Multiple imputation (m at least 20, more when more rows are incomplete)
methods.customary: Customary in epidemiology (Sterne et al. 2009, BMJ 338:b2393)
methods.sound: Sound: with the outcome and energy in the imputation model it is unbiased under missing at random and its intervals carry the imputation's uncertainty (Moons et al. 2006).

methods.label: Complete cases
methods.customary: Customary in epidemiology; most software's default
methods.sound: Sound if complete cases give unbiased coefficients only if whether a value is missing does not depend on the outcome, given the predictors (Groenwold et al. 2012; White & Carlin 2010); it costs every incomplete row.

methods.label: Single fill in each training fold
methods.customary: Customary in machine-learning pipelines (scikit-learn's SimpleImputer)
methods.sound: Unsound for an interval: a single fill treats each imputed value as measured, so the intervals are too narrow, and a median fill biases a coefficient whenever who is missing depends on another variable.

methods.label: Single fill with missing indicators
methods.customary: Customary in prediction from health records (Sperrin et al. 2020)
methods.sound: Unsound for an estimate: the missing-indicator method almost always biases the estimates of a nonrandomized study (Groenwold et al. 2012); it is valid for baseline covariates in a randomized trial.

methods.label: Blanks as their own level
methods.customary: Customary for questions not asked (a blank medication answer)
methods.sound: The missing-indicator method for categories: the missing-indicator method almost always biases the estimates of a nonrandomized study (Groenwold et al. 2012); it is valid for baseline covariates in a randomized trial; sound when a blank means not asked (then it is a value, not missing).

below_detection.label: Censoring-aware
below_detection.customary: Less common in metabolomics; the epidemiology of exposures below detection (Lubin et al. 2004)
below_detection.sound: Sound for associations. A censored-normal (Tobit) draw below the limit within the multiple imputation, given the outcome (Lubin et al. 2004).

below_detection.label: Half the smallest detected value
below_detection.sound: Biased for associations as censoring grows, and collapses every non-detect to one value (Lubin et al. 2004: biased unless 5–10% are below the limit).

below_detection.label: As any other blank (the median fill)
below_detection.sound: Unsound: the median places non-detections in the middle of the distribution.

imputation_models.label: Compatible with the analysis model (SMC-FCS where the model needs it)
imputation_models.customary: Chained equations with derived terms made in each copy (passive) are the field's habit (mice's and Stata's defaults)
imputation_models.sound: Sound: SMC-FCS where the model holds a spline, a log, a ratio or a logistic or Cox outcome, chained equations where it is linear in the imputed values (Bartlett et al. 2015)

imputation_models.label: Passive: terms derived in each completed copy
imputation_models.customary: Customary: mice's and Stata's ice defaults derive transformed and product terms in each completed copy
imputation_models.sound: Unsound with a declared nonlinear term: passive imputation draws each value from a model linear in it and only then derives the declared nonlinear terms, so the curvature and the nonlinearity tests would be biased toward the null (Bartlett et al. 2015)

imputation_models.label: Single-level on clustered rows
imputation_models.customary: Customary: chained equations that ignore the clustering
imputation_models.sound: Unsound on clustered rows: imputing clustered rows one at a time gives a unit's time-invariant values different draws on its different rows and erases the correlation within units (Lüdtke, Robitzsch & Grund 2017)

exposure_forms.label: Restricted cubic spline
exposure_forms.customary: Increasingly customary in nutritional epidemiology: "now near-default" (NUTRITION_PACK §07G; Desquilbet & Mariotti 2010).
exposure_forms.sound: Sound: a smooth curve with few parameters, linear in the tails, with a test of nonlinearity; knots at Harrell's percentiles of the fitting rows.

exposure_forms.label: Straight line
exposure_forms.customary: Customary: one coefficient per unit of intake.
exposure_forms.sound: Sound when the relation is close to a line; a curve it misses biases the slope.

exposure_forms.label: Quintiles with a trend test
exposure_forms.customary: Customary in nutritional epidemiology: "quintiles remain expected alongside" the spline (NUTRITION_PACK §07G).
exposure_forms.sound: Weaker for inference: cutting a continuous intake into fifths discards the variation within each fifth and assumes a step at each cut; the trend test scores each fifth by its median.
exposure_forms.consequence: Four indicators against the lowest fifth, and a trend across medians.

families.label: Linear model
families.inductive_bias: Each predictor adds a straight-line effect; effects add up, with no interactions unless you build them.

families.label: Elastic net
concerns: Penalized coefficients are shrunk and carry no confidence intervals.
families.inductive_bias: Straight-line effects shrunk toward zero; few predictors matter, correlated ones share weight.

families.label: Feature-wise regression
concerns: Each exposure is adjusted for the covariates but not for the other exposures: a separate question for each.
families.inductive_bias: Each exposure tested on its own with the covariates; Benjamini–Hochberg holds the false-discovery rate.

families.label: Boosted trees
concerns: No coefficients or intervals: effects are read from curves instead.
families.inductive_bias: Effects are step functions that can bend and interact; many shallow trees each correct the last.

families.label: Random-intercept mixed model
concerns: No identifier repeats in these rows, so there is no unit for a random intercept; it is the linear model's fit.
families.inductive_bias: Straight-line effects, plus a level of its own for each unit whose rows repeat.

families.label: GEE (exchangeable)
concerns: No identifier repeats in these rows, so there is no within-unit correlation to model; it is the linear model's fit.
families.inductive_bias: Population-average straight-line or log-odds effects; a unit's rows share one correlation.

families.label: Screened elastic net
concerns: Screening chooses the reported features from the outcome: under inference that is selection, refused for the reported model.
families.inductive_bias: Only features with a strong marginal association survive; among them, straight-line effects shrunk toward zero.

methods.label: Complete cases

exposure_forms.label: Restricted cubic spline

exposure_forms.sound: Sound: a smooth curve with few parameters, linear in the tails, with a test of nonlinearity; knots at Harrell's percentiles of the fitting rows.

exposure_forms.label: Straight line
exposure_forms.customary: Customary: one coefficient per unit of intake.
exposure_forms.sound: Sound when the relation is close to a line; a curve it misses biases the slope.
exposure_forms.consequence: One coefficient per unit; no curvature.

exposure_forms.label: Quintiles with a trend test
exposure_forms.customary: Customary in nutritional epidemiology: "quintiles remain expected alongside" the spline (NUTRITION_PACK §07G).
exposure_forms.sound: Weaker for inference: cutting a continuous intake into fifths discards the variation within each fifth and assumes a step at each cut; the trend test scores each fifth by its median.
exposure_forms.consequence: Four indicators against the lowest fifth, and a trend across medians.

families.label: Linear model
families.inductive_bias: Each predictor adds a straight-line effect; effects add up, with no interactions unless you build them.

families.label: Elastic net
concerns: Penalized coefficients are shrunk and carry no confidence intervals.
families.inductive_bias: Straight-line effects shrunk toward zero; few predictors matter, correlated ones share weight.

families.label: Feature-wise regression
concerns: Each exposure is adjusted for the covariates but not for the other exposures: a separate question for each.
families.inductive_bias: Each exposure tested on its own with the covariates; Benjamini–Hochberg holds the false-discovery rate.

families.label: Boosted trees
concerns: No coefficients or intervals: effects are read from curves instead.
families.inductive_bias: Effects are step functions that can bend and interact; many shallow trees each correct the last.

families.label: Random-intercept mixed model
concerns: No identifier repeats in these rows, so there is no unit for a random intercept; it is the linear model's fit.
families.inductive_bias: Straight-line effects, plus a level of its own for each unit whose rows repeat.

families.label: GEE (exchangeable)
concerns: No identifier repeats in these rows, so there is no within-unit correlation to model; it is the linear model's fit.
families.inductive_bias: Population-average straight-line or log-odds effects; a unit's rows share one correlation.

families.label: Screened elastic net
concerns: Screening chooses the reported features from the outcome: under inference that is selection, refused for the reported model.
families.inductive_bias: Only features with a strong marginal association survive; among them, straight-line effects shrunk toward zero.

families.label: Linear model
families.inductive_bias: Each predictor adds a straight-line effect; effects add up, with no interactions unless you build them.

families.label: Elastic net
concerns: Penalized coefficients are shrunk and carry no confidence intervals.
families.inductive_bias: Straight-line effects shrunk toward zero; few predictors matter, correlated ones share weight.

families.label: Feature-wise regression
concerns: Each exposure is adjusted for the covariates but not for the other exposures: a separate question for each.
families.inductive_bias: Each exposure tested on its own with the covariates; Benjamini–Hochberg holds the false-discovery rate.

families.label: Boosted trees
concerns: No coefficients or intervals: effects are read from curves instead.
families.inductive_bias: Effects are step functions that can bend and interact; many shallow trees each correct the last.

families.label: Random-intercept mixed model
concerns: No identifier repeats in these rows, so there is no unit for a random intercept; it is the linear model's fit.
families.inductive_bias: Straight-line effects, plus a level of its own for each unit whose rows repeat.

families.label: GEE (exchangeable)
concerns: No identifier repeats in these rows, so there is no within-unit correlation to model; it is the linear model's fit.
families.inductive_bias: Population-average straight-line or log-odds effects; a unit's rows share one correlation.

families.label: Screened elastic net
concerns: Screening chooses the reported features from the outcome: under inference that is selection, refused for the reported model.
families.inductive_bias: Only features with a strong marginal association survive; among them, straight-line effects shrunk toward zero.

steps.label: Ordinary least squares
steps.detail: Fits the straight-line effect of every column. The coefficient table uses every analyzed row; intervals use HC3 robust standard errors, or CR2 cluster-robust ones when a unit's rows repeat, or Taylor linearization over a survey design.

artifact.estimand: More of each nutrient with total energy held fixed: with protein, carbohydrate and fat all in the model, each coefficient is a substitution in place of the energy sources not in the model: alcohol, other. It is not a swap for the average of all other sources (NUTRITION_PACK §05a: name the omitted component). carb sits beside its own parts sugar, so its coefficient is the remaining carbohydrate (holding sugar fixed): the carbohydrate in none of them, not total carbohydrate. fat_total sits beside its own parts fat_sat, fat_mon and fat_poly, so its coefficient is the remaining fat (holding fat_sat, fat_mon, fat_poly fixed): the fat in none of them, not total fat.
warnings: sugar is a part of carb: carb's coefficient is the remainder (holding sugar fixed), not total carb; leave it out to estimate the total. A substitution through carb moves it in proportion, and never pairs carb with its own part.

fat_sat, fat_mon, fat_poly are parts of fat_total: fat_total's coefficient is the remainder (holding fat_sat, fat_mon, fat_poly fixed), not total fat_total; leave them out to estimate the total. A substitution through fat_total moves them in proportion, and never pairs fat_total with its own part.

artifact.cv_definition: Cross-validated R², MSE, RMSE and MAE pool every out-of-fold prediction; R² is measured against the mean of the rows each fold's model was fit on, as the held-out R² is against the training rows' mean. The fold values show the spread.
artifact.se_definition: Each standard error counts which rows were scored, with each fold's model as fitted (LeDell et al. 2015; DeLong's for the AUC); it leaves out how the models would vary with other training rows.

diagnostics.method: Leverage and Cook's distance of every row, as R's hatvalues and cooks.distance give them, against the median of F(19, 21,830) = 0.965 (Cook 1977, Technometrics 19:15)
diagnostics.reading: No row moves the estimates past Cook's reference (largest distance 0.0399, against 0.965).

robustness.interval_note: The robustness value for the 95% interval and the benchmarks' adjusted intervals rest on the classical least-squares standard error (0.00592), as sensemakr computes them; the interval reported uses HC3 standard errors, 0.00651, so they are not reported: they would describe an interval that is not the one shown.

sensitivity.reading: An unmeasured confounder would need a partial R² of 2.3% with both `sugar` and `glucose`, beyond the measured covariates, to bring the estimate to zero (Cinelli & Hazlett 2020, J R Stat Soc B 82:39); one as strong as `carb` would move it to 0.03358. The robustness value for the 95% interval and the benchmarks' adjusted intervals rest on the classical least-squares standard error (0.00592), as sensemakr computes them; the interval reported uses HC3 standard errors, 0.00651, so they are not reported: they would describe an interval that is not the one shown. E-value for the estimate: 1.02, and for the confidence limit nearer the null 1.01 (VanderWeele & Ding 2017, Ann Intern Med 167:268); an E-value is read against the confounders one can name, never as a pass or a fail.

artifact.methods: The estimate of `sugar` is reported across a declared sequence of models fit on all 21,849 analyzed rows: unadjusted; Model 1, adjusted for `age`, `gender` and `kcal`; Model 2, the primary, adjusted for `cycle_begin_year`, `age`, `gender`, `kcal`, `protein`, `carb`, `fat_total` and 3 more; Model 3, further adjusted for `weight`, `height`, `bmi` and `waist`, possible mediators, so not a total effect. Only the exposure's estimates are shown as effects; every other coefficient is listed apart as an adjustment term, not an effect estimate (Westreich & Greenland 2013, Am J Epidemiol 177:292). Influence was checked by Cook's distance against the median of F(19, 21,830) (Cook 1977, Technometrics 19:15): 0 rows above it. Sensitivity to unmeasured confounding is reported by the Cinelli–Hazlett robustness value (each adjusted covariate a named benchmark; its form for the 95% interval, and the benchmarks' intervals, are not reported, as they assume classical standard errors and the intervals reported are HC3) and by the E-value for the estimate and for the confidence limit nearer the null, never as a pass or a fail.
